FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards after the draft finalized by the Photographic Materials Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. 2-Amino-5-l N-ethyl N-2, hydroxy ethyl ] aminotoluene sulphate, photographic grade ( CD-4 ) is used as a photographic colour developer. It is also known in the trade by names like colour developer-4 or CD-4. It has the following structural formula:

( Molecular Mass = 291'35)

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised 1'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

2-AMINO-5-[ N-ETHYL N-2, HYDROXY ETHYL ] AMINOTOLUENE SULPHATE. PHOTOGRAPHIC GRADE ( CD-4 )
1 SCOPE This standard prescribes the requirements and the methods of sampling and test for 2-amino-5 [ N-ethyl N-2, hydroxy ethyl 1 aminotoluene sulphate, photographic grade ( CD-4) used as the basic constituent of developing solutions for treatment of multilayer light sensitive materials of colour photography. 2 REFERENCES The Indian Standards listed below necessary adjuncts to this standard: IS No. 1070 : 1977 2263 : 1979 Title Water for general ( seconn revision ) laboratory use The material shall be packed in suitable, dark coloured airtight bottles or as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier, 4.2 Marking The containers marked legibly information: shall be securely closed and and indelibly with the following are the 3.2 Solution in Water A freshly prepared solution of the material containing 5 g of the sample in 100 ml of water shall be clear and free from sediments. 3.3 The material shall comply with the requirements prescribed in Table 1 when tested according to the methods given in Annex A. Reference to the relevant clauses of Annex A is given in co1 4 of Table 1. 4 PACKING, MARKING PRECAUTlONS 4.1 Packing AND SAFETY

IS 13104 : 1991 4.3 Safety Precautions 2-Amino-5-[ N-ethyl N-2, hydroxy ethyl 1 aminotoluene sulphate, photographic grade ( CD-4 ) has a pronounced general toxic action and shows particular effect on liver and central nervous system. On skin contact, it may cause eczema. 4.3.1 Work with 2-amino-5-[ N-ethyl N-2, hydroxy ethyl ] aminotoluene sulphate, photographic grade ( CD-4) should be done only with protective clothing. The place should be provided with exhaust and ventilation systems. 5 SAMPLING Representative samples of the material drawn and their conformity to the determined as prescribed in Annex B. shall be standard

Using standard ceric sulphate solution, the free base content is found out by volumetric method. A-2.1 A-2.1.1 A-2.1.2 Reagents Dilute Sulphuric Acid -

A-3.1.1 Barium Chloride Solution - approximately 10 percent ( m/v ). A-3.1.2 A-3.2 Concentrated Hydrochloric Acid Procedure

Weigh accurately about 1'25 g of sample in a 250-ml volumetric flask. Dissolve it in dilute sulphuric acid and make up to the mark with dilute sulphuric acid. A-2.2.1 In a 1 OOO-ml conical flask, take 100 ml of dilute hydrochloric acid and 200 ml of water and add 10 drops of ferroin indicator. Titrate with ceric sulphate solution to a pale blue end point. Record the blank titre value VI. Pipette out 50 ml of the sample solution prepared in A-2.2, into the conical flask and continue titration without refilling the burette until a loss of orange colour is observed momentarily. Reduce the rate of addition as end point is approached so that one drop is added every 3 to 4 seconds near the end point. The end point is of a greenish yellow colour which does not change with the addition of one more drop. Record the net titre value V. 2

Weigh accurately 5 & 0'1 g of the sample, transfer it to the lOO-ml volumetric flask, dissolve and make up to the mark using water, Pipette out 20 ml of this made-up solution into a 250-ml beaker containing 80 ml water and one millilitre of h_ydrochloric acid and heat to boil. To this hot solution, add about 10 ml of hot barium chloride solution, and continue stirring at boiling temperature for 2 minutes to complete to precipitation of barium sulphate. Continue heating on a water bath for 1-2 hours and filter through Whatman No. 40 filter paper. Wash the precipitate with hot water until the filtrate is free from chloride. Incinerate and ignite the precipitate in a tared silica crucible. Cool the crucible to room temperature and weigh to a constant mass.

A-4.2 Procedure Weigh accurately 5'0 g of the material and transfer to a tared silica crucible and then ignite at dull red heat ( approximately 600�C). Cool in a desiccator and weigh to constant mass. Preserve the residue for the determination of iron and heavy metals in A-5 and A-6. A-4.3 Calculation Ash, percent where iVl= ~2= by mass = Ml x 100 Mz

A-5.1.2.1 Add 5 ml of concentrated hydrochloric acid to the residue obtained from the determination of ash (see A-4) and evaporate to dryness. Dissolve the residue in 15 ml of dilute hydrochloric acid and warm on a steam-bath for 10 minutes. Cool, dilute to 50 ml with water in a volumetric flask and mix thoroughly. Use 20 ml of thus solution for the determination of iron and preserve the remaining solution for heavy metals test in A-6. A-5.1.2.2 Thoroughly mix equal parts of o-phenanthroline, hydroxylamine hydrochloride and acetate buffer ofpH 5. Add 5 ml of this mixture to each of 4 ml of the standard iron solution and 20 ml of sample solution. Dilute to 50 ml with water and mix well. A-5.1.2.3 The material shall be taken to have not exceeded the limit prescribed for iron, if the colour produced is not deeper than that produced by the standard iron solution. A-5 DETERMINATION A-5.0 General

Two methods have been prescribed for the determination of iron, namely (a) o-phenanthroline method. method, and (b) thioglycollic acid However, in case of dispute, the o-phenanthroline method shall be the referee method. A-5.1 A-5.1.0 o-Phenanthroline General Method

Concentrated hydrochloric acid is added to the residue obtained from the determination of ash, evaporated to dryness and finally dissolve in dilute hydrochloric acid. Thioglycollic acid is then added to the solution, the solution is made alkaline and the colour produced is compared with that produced by standard iron solution under identical conditions. A-6.2 Procedure A-6.2.1 To the 20 ml portion of the sample solution ( see A-5.1.2.1 ) in a Nessler cylinder, add a few drops of p-nitrophenol indicator and then add ammonium hydroxide dropwise, until the solution turns yellow. Add dilute hydrochloric acid dropwise, until the solution becomes colourless again and then add 0'5 ml in excess. Add 5 ml of hydrogen sulphide solution and dilute to 50 ml. A-6.2.2 At the same time transfer 5 ml of into another Nessler standard lead solution cylinder and make it neutral to p-nitrophenol indicator by using dilute ammonium hydroxide and dilute hydrochloric acid as described in A-6.2.1. Add 0'5 ml of dilute hydrochloric acid in excess and 5 ml of hydrogen sulphide solution. Dilute to 50 ml. A-6.2.3 The material shall be considered to have passed requirement of the test if' the colour produced in the sample solution is not deeper than that produced in the standard solution. 4

A-8.2 Procedure Prepare a five percent solution of the material in a IOO-ml beaker, using freshly boiled and cooled Measure the pH of the solution using a water. pH meter. A-9 IDENTITY A-9.1 Melting TEST Point Test

Assemble capillary tube melting point apparatus using a thermometer that covers the range IOO200�C. Prepare 3 capillary tubes, placing in them ( 1 ) the sample to be tested, ( 2 ) a sample known to be 2-amino-5-L N-ethyl N-2, hydroxy photographic sulphate, ethyl 1 aminotoluene grade, and ( 3 ) a finely ground mixture of ( I 1 and ( 2 ) mixed in the ratio of 1 : 1. Identify the tubes, attach them to the thermometer and insert in the tnelting point bath. Heat the bath to approximately 135�C and thereafter heat at a constant rate of 1�C per minute stirring constantly. Note the melting point of the contents of each tube as indicated by the first appearance of liquefaction. The melting point of the mixture shall be not lower than those of the two samples. The melting point of the sample should be between 156�C and 158�C.

ANNEX

B

( Clause 5.1 )
SAMPLING OF 2-AM[NO-5-l N-ETHYL N-2, HYDROXY ETHYL 1 AMINOTOLUENE SULPHATE, PHOTOGRAPHIC GRADE ( CD-4 ) B-l GENERAL SAMPLING REQUIREMENTS FOR Arrange all the containers in the lot in a systematic manner and, starting from any one, count them as 1, 2.. . . . . r, where r is the integral part of N/n ( N and n being the lot size and sample size respectively ). Every rth container thus counted shall be withdrawn to constitute the sample. B-3 PREPARATION B-3.1 Drawing OF TEST SAMPLES

B-l.1 In drawing, preparing, storing and ling test samples, the following precautions be observed. B-1.2 Samples shall not be taken exposed to weather. out at

handshall

a place

B-l.3 Precautions shall be taken to protect the samples, the material being sampled, the sampling instrument and the containers for samples from adventitious contamination. samples, B-l.4 To draw ~representative the contents of each container selected for sampling shall be mixed thoroughly by suitable means. B-l.5 The samples shall be placed clean, dry and airtight glass or plastic in suitable, containers. such a by the

of Samples sample from each container

Draw a representative selected.

B-3.1.1 Mix portions of the material drawn from the same container to prepare the test sample representing the container. The quantity of material to be drawn from each container shall be sufficient to conduct all the tests given in 3 and shall be not less than 200 g. B-3.1.2 The samples shall be stored in dry glass bottles or other suitable containers, sealed airtight and labelled with all the particulars of sampling given in B-1.7. B-3.2 The remaining portions of the material from each of the five containers shall be divided into three equal parts, each forming an individual sample. One set of individual samples, representing the container samples shall be marked for the purchaser, another for the supplier and the third to be used as a referee sample. B-3.3 All the individual and composite shall be immediately transferred to sample containers and labelled with full ation particulars. samples separate identific-

B-l.6 The sample containers shall be of size that they are almost completely filled sample.

B-l.7 Each sample container shall be sealed airtight after filling and marked with full details of sampling, the date of sampling and the year of manufacture. B-1.8 Samples shall be stored in such a manner that the temperature of the material does not vary unduly from the ambient temperature. B-2 SCALE B-2.1 Lot OF SAMPLING

All the containers in a single consignment of the material drawn from a single batch of manufacture shall constitute a lot. If a consignment is declared to consist of different batches, the batches shall be marked separately and the group of containers in each batch shall constitute a separate lot. B-2.2 From each lot five containers shall be selected ( see B-2.2.1 ) for drawing samples for test. In case the lot contains less than five containers, each container shall be tested. B-2.2.1 These containers shall be selected at random from the lot. In order to ensure the randomness of selection, procedure given in IS 4905 : 1968 may be followed. In case this standard is not available, the following procedure may be adopted:

B-3.4 The referee samples consisting of a composite sample and a set of individual samples, shall bear the seal of both the purchaser and the supplier. These shall be kept at a place agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier, to be used in case of dispute between the two. B-4 NUMBER OF TESTS base, each other shall

B-4.1 Tests for the determination of free heavy metals and iron shall be conducted on of the five individual samples. Tests for all characteristics prescribed in 2 and Table 1 be conducted on the composite sample.
